The caregiver clarified that no measuring was needed and guided the child to simply open the pantry, retrieve and open the kibble bag, and pour directly into the bowl. The child succeeded by following these steps independently and correctly.
  2. The child successfully retrieved the screwdriver from under the bathroom sink to address the loose hinge screw on the cabinet door, demonstrating understanding of the home repair task. The caregiver affirmed the correct first step and guided the child to proceed with tightening the screw. The task is ongoing, with success expected upon proper reattachment of the hinge.
  3. The task was an organizing activity requiring the child to slide a stack of unsorted mail into a designated sorting tray on the hallway desk. The child initially overcomplicated the task by considering irrelevant objects like magazines and coasters, struggling to identify the simple physical action needed. The caregiver clarified that no extra steps were necessary—just use hands to gently push the pre-stacked mail directly into the tray. The child succeeded by following this guidance and completing the task with focused, appropriate action.
